causal:influence:antithrombin:negative:t.evidence: Wajima 2009 (antithrombin inhibition), BioModels BIOMD0000000340; Boron & Boulpaep (antithrombin anticoagulant system) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-104 (18.6: Hemostasis): 'Antithrombin inactivates factor X and opposes the conversion of prothrombin (factor II) to thrombin in the common pathway'; Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-13.14 (Gap Junctions - Undeclared): 'Heparin... activating antithrombin III, which inhibits clotting' — corroborates antithrombin anticoagulant activity inhibiting thrombin; Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-7.2.5 (Glycosaminoglycans - Heteropolysaccharides with Disaccharide Repeating Units): 'Heparin acts as a catalyst to accelerate the inhibition of the enzyme thrombin... antithrombin III [inhibits thrombin]' — corroborates antithrombin inhibiting thrombin activity

causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:to.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. causal:influence:arterial_ph:positive:to.mechanism: lower pH (raised hydrogen ion) relaxes arteriolar smooth muscle; raising pH (lowering H+) conversely constricts arterioles, raising resistance

causal:influence:arterial_po2:positive:r.mechanism: higher arterial O2 tension raises renal arterial O2 content and thus tissue oxygenation

causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.evidence: MSUD (OMIM 248600); NBK557773 — accumulation of leucine, isoleucine, and valine; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18. | intervention: do(BCKDH complex activity ↓) = maple syrup urine disease (OMIM 248600)

causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.evidence: PMC11786200 (Persistent elevations of alkaline phosphatase as an early indicator of GM1 gangliosidosis; ALP significantly higher in infantile GM1 vs late-infantile/juvenile; associated with abnormal bone physiology in neonatal period); OMIM 230500 (GM1-gangliosidosis type I; GLB1 LoF; skeletal dysplasia); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Lysosomal Storage Diseases (GM1 gangliosidosis: hepatosplenomegaly, skeletal dysplasia, early death). | intervention: GLB1 biallelic loss-of-function (GM1 gangliosidosis, OMIM 230500): do(beta_galactosidase_activity DOWN) -> GM1 ganglioside / keratan sulfate accumulation in bone -> osteoblast dysregulation -> elevated serum alkaline phosphatase [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.mechanism: GLB1 deficiency (GM1 gangliosidosis) causes lysosomal storage of GM1 ganglioside and keratan sulfate in bone cells, inducing osteoblast dysfunction and reactive periosteal bone remodeling; serum alkaline phosphatase rises as an early biomarker of this abnormal bone physiology. More beta-galactosidase activity prevents storage, reduces bone pathology, and keeps alkaline phosphatase at baseline.

causal:influence:beta_hexosaminidase_b_a.evidence: PMID 28553389; (Sandhoff Disease without Hepatosplenomegaly Due to Hexosaminidase B Gene Mutation, abstract/introduction); “Sandhoff disease is a neurodegenerative disease caused due to deficiency of hexosaminidase (HEX) A and B.” | HEXB (beta-subunit) loss causes deficiency of both HexA and HexB, so loss of beta-hexosaminidase-B activity lowers total (serum) hexosaminidase, supporting beta_hexosaminidase_b_activity -> plasma_beta_hexosaminidase with sign +. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:beta_hexosaminidase_b_a.mechanism: The beta subunit (HEXB) is shared by both hexosaminidase isoenzymes (HexA = alpha-beta, HexB = beta-beta); biallelic HEXB loss-of-function (Sandhoff disease, a natural do()) abolishes both isoenzymes, so total serum beta-hexosaminidase falls - hence beta-hexosaminidase-B activity positively determines measured serum total hexosaminidase, joining the lysosomal HEX/GM2 island to the core serum analyte.

causal:influence:blood_urea_nitrogen:pos.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (urea recycling and the countercurrent multiplier; contribution of urea to maximal urine concentration)
causal:influence:blood_urea_nitrogen:pos.mechanism: urea recycling into the inner medulla contributes substantially to the medullary osmotic gradient that drives maximal urine concentration; higher delivered urea raises achievable urine osmolality

causal:influence:breast_milk_zinc:positi.evidence: OMIM 608118 (transient neonatal zinc deficiency, TNZD; SLC30A2 LoF in lactating mothers; infants present with immune insufficiency, dermatitis, diarrhoea); PMC3669329 (Itsumura et al. 2013, compound heterozygous SLC30A2 mutations: >75% reduction in breast milk zinc causing zinc deficiency with immune dysfunction in breastfed infant); PMC10030689 (novel SLC30A2 mutations in transient neonatal zinc deficiency: immune insufficiency explicitly listed); Prasad 1998 / PMC7199614 (experimental human zinc deficiency: decreased thymulin activity in Th1, decreased mRNA of IL-2 and IFN-gamma, decreased NK and cytotoxic T-cell activity); ScienceDirect (zinc deficiency, depressed thymic hormones, and T lymphocyte dysfunction; thymic involution and lymphopenia as classic hallmarks); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (zinc deficiency: impaired cellular immunity, thymic involution, depressed cell-mediated immunity). | intervention: SLC30A2 loss-of-function in lactating mother (OMIM 608118) causing infant zinc deficiency | intervention: SLC30A2/ZnT2 loss-of-function in lactating mother (OMIM 608118) causing transient neonatal zinc deficiency
causal:influence:breast_milk_zinc:positi.mechanism: Zinc is an obligate cofactor for thymulin (a thymic nonapeptide hormone) and is required for T-cell differentiation, thymic epithelial integrity, and IL-2-dependent T-cell proliferation. When breast milk zinc is low due to SLC30A2/ZnT2 LoF in the mother, the nursing infant develops transient neonatal zinc deficiency; zinc depletion causes thymic involution, depressed thymulin activity, lymphopenia, reduced IL-2 and IFN-gamma production, and impaired T-cell cytotoxic function. Infant T-cell mediated immune activity falls proportionally to the severity and duration of zinc deficiency. Intervention: do(SLC30A2 LoF in lactating mother) -> low breast milk zinc -> infant zinc deficiency -> thymic atrophy, reduced thymulin saturation -> low T-cell immune activity.

causal:influence:bronchiole_smooth_muscl.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-124 (22.2: Organs and Structures of the Respiratory System): 'This muscular wall can change the size of the tubing to increase or decrease airflow through the tube'; asthma section: 'bronchospasms (constriction of the bronchioles), which can inhibit air from entering the lungs' — the canonical do() is bronchial provocation (methacholine challenge), which increases smooth-muscle tone and raises measured airway resistance (PD20/PC20 endpoints in spirometry). | intervention: Methacholine challenge / do(bronchiole_smooth_muscle_tone +): FEV1 falls and airway resistance rises; β2-agonist bronchodilator / do(bronchiole_smooth_muscle_tone -): resistance falls (standard spirometric reversibility testing)
causal:influence:bronchiole_smooth_muscl.mechanism: Bronchiole smooth muscle contraction (bronchoconstriction) reduces luminal radius; by the Hagen–Poiseuille relationship airway resistance scales as r⁻⁴, so even modest narrowing dramatically increases resistance to airflow. Conversely, bronchodilation reduces resistance.

causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.evidence: XLA (OMIM 300755): absent IgG including all subclasses; Janeway's Immunobiology 10th ed.; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine. | intervention: do(BTK LoF) — no IgG3-secreting plasma cells
causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.mechanism: BTK deficiency prevents all B cell maturation; IgG3 — like all IgG subclasses — is absent in XLA.

causal:influence:cardiac_output:positive.evidence: West JB Respiratory Physiology 9th ed (Fick principle: pulmonary blood flow = cardiac output in the absence of shunts). Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (pulmonary circulation: entire right heart output perfuses the lung). Guyton & Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology 13th ed Ch. 38: 'the quantity of blood flowing through the lungs is approximately equal to the cardiac output'. | intervention: Perturbation: exercise raises cardiac output 4–6 fold → proportional increase in pulmonary perfusion (confirmed by indicator-dilution pulmonary blood flow measurements at rest vs. exercise).
causal:influence:cardiac_output:positive.mechanism: In the normal pulmonary circulation, all cardiac output passes through the pulmonary capillary bed (assuming no right-to-left shunt); pulmonary capillary perfusion rate equals cardiac output (Fick principle). An increase in cardiac output directly raises the rate of blood flow through the pulmonary capillaries.

causal:influence:cardiac_output:positive.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.19 (Dominant Role of the Kidney in Long-Term Pressure Control) §Increased Fluid Volume Can Elevate Arterial Pressure: “When increased blood volume increases the cardiac output, the blood flow increases in all tissues of the body, so that this autoregulation mechanism constricts blood vessels all over the body. This in turn increases the total peripheral resistance”
causal:influence:cardiac_output:positive.mechanism: excess cardiac output raises tissue blood flow, the disposition of local arterioles to autoregulate drives the constriction process, raising whole-body resistance

causal:influence:casr_activity:negative:.mechanism: CaSR detects extracellular ionized calcium; active CaSR suppresses PTH secretion; inactivating CaSR mutations (LoF) reduce the calcium set-point for PTH suppression, causing hypercalcemia from inadequate PTH suppression

causal:influence:cd40l_signaling_activit.evidence: HIGM1 (OMIM 308230): absent serum IgA; Janeway's Immunobiology 10th ed., 'T cell-dependent B cell responses'; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine. | intervention: do(CD40LG LoF) — no class-switch to IgA; IgA absent in HIGM1
causal:influence:cd40l_signaling_activit.mechanism: CD40–CD40L costimulation is required for class-switch recombination to IgA; CD40L deficiency abolishes IgA production.

causal:influence:cellular_cobalamin_upta.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (cobalamin coenzymes: adenosylcobalamin for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase); intracellular cobalamin-processing disorders (cblA/cblB) reduce adenosylcobalamin
causal:influence:cellular_cobalamin_upta.mechanism: intracellular cobalamin (from cellular uptake) is processed in mitochondria to adenosylcobalamin (the methylmalonyl-CoA-mutase coenzyme); reduced cobalamin uptake lowers adenosylcobalamin

Loss of CFTR activity (cystic fibrosis, CFTR LoF) abolishes ductal chloride reabsorption, so sweat chloride rises. do(CFTR_activity down) → sweat_chloride up.

causal:influence:core_temperature:positi.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-004 (1.5: Requirements for Human Life): 'controlled hypothermia... decreases the metabolic needs of the brain, heart, and other organs' and 'slows the patient's metabolic rate'; also: 'chemical reactions upon which the body depends can only take place within a narrow range of body temperature'.
causal:influence:core_temperature:positi.mechanism: Temperature sets the rate of enzyme-catalysed metabolic reactions; controlled hypothermia (reduced core temperature) decreases whole-body metabolic rate, while hyperthermia raises it (Q10 effect on cellular chemistry).

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:il1be.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (glucocorticoid suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines); Janeway's Immunobiology
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:il1be.mechanism: glucocorticoids inhibit NF-kB/AP-1-driven IL-1beta transcription and promote anti-inflammatory mediators

CTNS LoF (cystinosis) abolishes lysosomal cystine export, causing intralysosomal cystine crystals to accumulate throughout cells; intracellular (lysosomal) cystine concentration rises markedly.

causal:influence:dbh_activity:positive:n.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (dopamine --DBH--> norepinephrine); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (dopamine-beta-hydroxylase deficiency, OMIM 223360: undetectable plasma norepinephrine/epinephrine); pathognomonic natural human LoF: plasma NE undetectable (<25 pg/mL) and restored by droxidopa (a NE precursor bypassing DBH), confirming do(DBH)->norepinephrine sign '+' (GeneReviews NBK1474, DBH Deficiency; OMIM 223360)

causal:influence:dihydropyrimidine_dehyd.evidence: DPD deficiency OMIM 274270; van Kuilenburg et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2001 (DPD deficiency: persistent urinary and plasma excretion of uracil, thymine, and 5-hydroxymethyluracil); Saif et al., Cancer Chemother Pharmacol 2010. | intervention: do(DPYD LoF, DPD deficiency OMIM 274270) — thymine catabolism blocked; 5-HMU accumulates in plasma
causal:influence:dihydropyrimidine_dehyd.mechanism: 5-Hydroxymethyluracil (5-HMU) is a minor thymine metabolite formed by hydroxylation; in DPD deficiency, normal thymine catabolism is blocked, and thymine and its minor oxidative metabolite 5-HMU both accumulate in plasma.

causal:influence:dmgdh_activity:negative.evidence: DMGDH deficiency (OMIM 605850); PMC1275637 (AJHG 2001) — 'the concentration of N,N-dimethylglycine (DMG) was increased approximately 100-fold in the serum' in DMGDH deficiency; Clinical Chemistry PubMed 10102904 — NMR spectroscopy study confirming DMGDH deficiency as new inborn error of metabolism with markedly elevated DMG. | intervention: do(DMGDH activity ↓) = dimethylglycine dehydrogenase deficiency (OMIM 605850) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:dmgdh_activity:negative.mechanism: Dimethylglycine dehydrogenase (DMGDH) oxidatively demethylates N,N-dimethylglycine to sarcosine, using FAD as cofactor. Reduced DMGDH activity → dimethylglycine not cleared → plasma concentration rises approximately 100-fold (∂[DMG]/∂(DMGDH activity) < 0).

causal:influence:dmgdh_activity:positive.evidence: DMGDH deficiency OMIM 605850; Porter DH et al., J Biol Chem 1985 (DMGDH isolated from mitochondria; FAD reoxidation by ETF); PMC1275637 (AJHG 2005) — DMGDH deficiency with ~100-fold elevation of dimethylglycine; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (mitochondrial electron transport, ETF for fatty acid / amino acid oxidation). | intervention: do(DMGDH loss-of-function) — dimethylglycinuria / DMGDH deficiency OMIM 605850 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:dmgdh_activity:positive.mechanism: Dimethylglycine dehydrogenase (DMGDH) is a mitochondrial FAD-dependent oxidoreductase that catalyzes the oxidative demethylation of N,N-dimethylglycine to sarcosine. The FADH2 generated is transferred to the mitochondrial electron-transfer flavoprotein (ETF), donating electrons to ETF-ubiquinone oxidoreductase and thence to ubiquinol-complex III of the respiratory chain, ultimately driving ATP synthesis. DMGDH LoF reduces this electron-donating flux, slightly lowering mitochondrial ATP production in liver cells where DMGDH is most active. do(DMGDH LoF) → FADH2 from DMG catabolism absent → reduced mitochondrial electron input → cellular ATP ↓ (slight).

causal:influence:echs1_activity:negative.evidence: Haack et al. (PMC5947294) and Yamada et al. (PMC6996175) — clinical, biochemical and genetic features of ECHS1 deficiency (OMIM 616277): elevated urinary 2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutyrate confirmed in all patients; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases (short-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase deficiency) | intervention: Short-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase 1 deficiency (ECHS1 loss-of-function, OMIM 616277)
causal:influence:echs1_activity:negative.mechanism: ECHS1 hydrates methacrylyl-CoA to 3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA in valine catabolism; deficiency causes methacrylyl-CoA accumulation which is further metabolised to 2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutanoic acid (erythro-2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutyrate), the hallmark urinary marker — reduced ECHS1 activity raises urinary 2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutyrate

causal:influence:efferent_arteriolar_res.mechanism: efferent constriction raises total renal vascular resistance, reducing renal blood flow

causal:influence:glcnac_phosphotransfera.evidence: Kollmann K et al. J Bone Miner Res 2013 PMID:24127423 PMC3914524 'Decreased bone formation and increased osteoclastogenesis cause bone loss in mucolipidosis II' (GNPTAB knock-in mice: dysfunctional osteoblasts produce >5-fold elevated IL-6 driving RANKL-independent osteoclastogenesis; human ML-II bone biopsy confirms elevated osteoclast numbers; storage material accumulation in chondrocytes/osteoblasts confirmed); Mucolipidosis II alpha/beta OMIM:252500. | intervention: do(GNPTAB LoF = ML-II/I-cell disease OMIM:252500) -> GlcNAc-phosphotransferase activity falls -> osteoblast IL-6 up -> RANKL-independent osteoclastogenesis -> osteoclast_activity increases. | intervention: do(GNPTAB LoF = mucolipidosis II OMIM:252500) -> glcnac_phosphotransferase_activity falls -> osteoclast_activity increases [citations PubMed-verified]

Lysosome-deficient osteoblasts accumulate storage material and produce markedly elevated IL-6 (>5-fold) via a RANKL-independent mechanism, which drives excessive osteoclastogenesis. Reduced GlcNAc-phosphotransferase activity (LoF) -> osteoblast lysosomal dysfunction + IL-6 -> RANKL-independent osteoclast recruitment -> osteoclast activity up. Sign is negative: lower enzyme activity -> higher osteoclast activity.

causal:influence:glut4_membrane_transloc.evidence: Sedaghat et al. 2002, Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 283:E1084 (PMID 12376338; BioModels BIOMD0000000137); Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology.

causal:influence:glutamate_dehydrogenase.evidence: Hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome (HI/HA), OMIM:606762 — GLUD1 GoF increases glutamate catabolism; plasma glutamine may be mildly reduced or normal; edge encodes the physiological relationship (more enzyme -> less substrate)
causal:influence:glutamate_dehydrogenase.mechanism: RHEA:11612 (EC 1.4.1.3): L-glutamate + NADP(+) + H2O = 2-oxoglutarate + NH4(+) + NADPH; L-glutamate is the substrate; increased GLUD1 flux (GoF) depletes glutamate; glutamate is the immediate precursor of glutamine (via glutamine synthetase) so glutamate depletion leads to relative glutamine reduction or prevents its rise

causal:influence:glutamate_dehydrogenase.evidence: "Activating, dominantly inherited mutations of the glutamate dehydrogenase gene cause hyperinsulinemia and hyperammonemia syndrome, the second most common form of congenital hyperinsulinism. Hypoglycemia typically develops after several months of life and is responsive to diazoxide." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 38, p 1550
causal:influence:glutamate_dehydrogenase.mechanism: activating mutations of glutamate dehydrogenase (GLUD1) increase oxidative glutamate deamination in beta-cell mitochondria, raising the ATP/ADP ratio via alpha-ketoglutarate entry into the TCA cycle, stimulating insulin secretion; leucine also activates this pathway

causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.evidence: Congenital glutamine synthetase deficiency, OMIM:610015 — LoF reduces ammonia disposal via glutamine synthesis, causing hyperammonemia
causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.mechanism: RHEA:16169 (EC 6.3.1.2): L-glutamate + NH4(+) (CHEBI:28938) + ATP = L-glutamine + ADP + phosphate + H(+); ammonium/ammonia is a substrate consumed in glutamine synthesis

causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.evidence: Congenital glutamine synthetase deficiency, OMIM:610015 — LoF causes elevated plasma glutamate as the unconverted substrate accumulates
causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.mechanism: RHEA:16169 (EC 6.3.1.2): L-glutamate (CHEBI:29985) + NH4(+) + ATP = L-glutamine + ADP + phosphate + H(+); L-glutamate is the primary substrate

causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.evidence: Congenital glutamine synthetase deficiency, OMIM:610015 — LoF causes markedly low plasma glutamine, a defining metabolic feature
causal:influence:glutamine_synthetase_ac.mechanism: RHEA:16169 (EC 6.3.1.2): L-glutamate + NH4(+) + ATP = L-glutamine + ADP + phosphate + H(+); L-glutamine (CHEBI:58359) is the product of glutamine synthetase

causal:influence:glutathione_reductase_a.evidence: Orphanet ORPHA:90030 (Hemolytic anemia due to glutathione reductase deficiency — rare autosomal recessive, hemolytic crises on oxidative challenge); ScienceDirect (Familial Deficiency of Glutathione Reductase in Human Blood Cells — hemolysis, oxidative stress); PMID 2195189 (Impaired glutathione metabolism in hemolytic anemia — GSH depletion drives hemolysis). | intervention: do(GSR LoF) — biallelic GSR mutations causing hereditary hemolytic anemia (Orphanet ORPHA:90030) with GSSG accumulation and reduced red cell mass | intervention: do(glutathione_reductase/GSR loss-of-function) — biallelic GSR mutations causing hereditary hemolytic anemia (Orphanet ORPHA:90030) with oxidative hemolysis and reduced red cell mass [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:glutathione_reductase_a.mechanism: Glutathione reductase (GSR) reduces oxidized glutathione (GSSG) back to reduced glutathione (GSH) in the NADPH-dependent glutathione redox cycle. This is the principal mechanism for regenerating the erythrocyte's main antioxidant, GSH. GSR deficiency causes GSSG accumulation and GSH depletion in red blood cells; compromised antioxidant capacity leaves hemoglobin and membrane proteins vulnerable to oxidative damage, triggering hemolytic crises (especially upon oxidative challenge, e.g. fava bean ingestion). Hereditary complete GSR deficiency causes chronic hemolytic anemia, reducing total red cell mass. do(GSR activity up) → GSH regenerated → antioxidant capacity maintained → red_cell_mass preserved.

causal:influence:hal_activity:negative:p.evidence: Histidinemia (OMIM 235800); MedlinePlus Genetics — 'Histidinemia is a rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme histidase (HAL gene), which normally converts the amino acid histidine to urocanic acid'; NORD — 'Biochemical hallmarks are elevated histidine in blood, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 22 (histidine catabolism, HAL step). | intervention: do(HAL activity ↓) = histidinemia (OMIM 235800)
causal:influence:hal_activity:negative:p.mechanism: Histidine ammonia-lyase (HAL / histidase) irreversibly deaminates histidine to urocanate + ammonia; it is the sole enzyme catabolising the histidine carbon skeleton. Reduced HAL activity (histidinemia) → histidine not cleared → plasma histidine accumulates (∂[His]/∂(HAL activity) < 0).

causal:influence:helper_t_cell_activatio.evidence: Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-16.8 (The Immune System - Undeclared): 'The activated helper T-cell binds to and activates a B cell that has also bound to the antigen of interest, leading to massive B-cell proliferation'
causal:influence:helper_t_cell_activatio.mechanism: Activated helper T cell binds to and activates a B cell that has also bound to the same antigen, leading to massive B-cell proliferation

causal:influence:hgd_activity:negative:u.evidence: OMIM 203500 (alkaptonuria, HGD gene OMIM 607474): darkening urine due to homogentisic acid excretion is pathognomonic; Scriver et al., OMMBID; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases (alkaptonuria, HGD deficiency); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 | intervention: Alkaptonuria (HGD loss-of-function, OMIM 203500)

causal:influence:hibch_activity:positive.evidence: HIBCH deficiency (OMIM 250620); Reuter et al., Am J Med Genet 2014 (PMID 25251209): 'multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme deficiencies in skeletal muscle and fibroblasts'; Olsen et al., Clin Genet 2014 (PMC4222069): 'HIBCH mutations can cause Leigh-like disease with combined deficiency of multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain enzymes and pyruvate dehydrogenase'; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases. causal:influence:hibch_activity:positive.mechanism: 3-Hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA hydrolase (HIBCH) hydrolyzes 3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA to free 3-hydroxyisobutyrate and CoA in valine catabolism. HIBCH deficiency (OMIM 250620) causes upstream accumulation of methacrylyl-CoA, a reactive alpha,beta-unsaturated thioester that alkylates CoA pools and mitochondrial proteins, causing secondary deficiency of multiple respiratory chain complexes (I, III, and IV documented in muscle and fibroblasts). Do(HIBCH LoF) -> methacrylyl-CoA accumulates -> inhibits mitochondrial respiratory chain -> mitochondrial_respiratory_chain_activity decreases. HIBCH active -> methacrylyl-CoA cleared -> respiratory chain intact.

causal:influence:il1beta:positive:fecal_.evidence: Burtis & Ashwood Tietz Textbook (fecal calprotectin as a marker of intestinal neutrophil infiltration); Poullis et al. 2002 PMC6370282 (elevated fecal calprotectin is proportional to intestinal mucosal neutrophil number, validated in IBD); Janeway's Immunobiology (IL-1beta recruits and activates neutrophils at sites of intestinal inflammation). | intervention: IL-1beta elevation in IBD / intestinal inflammation — recruits intestinal neutrophils which release calprotectin into the gut lumen, raising fecal calprotectin.

causal:influence:il6:positive:plasma_hap.evidence: Burtis & Ashwood Tietz Textbook of Clinical Chemistry & Molecular Diagnostics (haptoglobin as a positive acute-phase reactant induced by IL-6); Nielsen & Moestrup 2009 (haptoglobin-CD163-HO-1 pathway regulated by IL-6, PMC3678498); Acute-phase protein synthesis in human hepatoma cells: SAA and haptoglobin regulated by IL-1 and IL-6, PMID 1706240. | intervention: IL-6 pharmacological elevation (e.g. IL-6 infusion or tocilizumab withdrawal) — directly upregulates hepatic haptoglobin synthesis 2–4-fold. causal:influence:intestinal_mucosal_perm.evidence: Crossley & Elliott 1977 (Diagnosis of protein-losing enteropathy by gastrointestinal clearance of alpha1-antitrypsin, PMID 80688); Florent et al. 1981 (intestinal clearance of alpha-1-antitrypsin as a sensitive method for protein-losing enteropathy, PMID 6973500); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (fecal AAT clearance as the diagnostic gold standard for protein-losing enteropathy). | intervention: do(inflammatory bowel disease / increased intestinal permeability) — protein-losing enteropathy: plasma protein including AAT crosses the inflamed mucosa into the intestinal lumen, raising fecal AAT. causal:influence:intracellular_atp:negat.evidence: Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-3.4 (Regulation of Enzyme Activity): 'if there are high enough levels of ATP in the cell that other cellular processes aren't using, then it can bind to phosphofructokinase outside of its active site... and turn it off. causal:influence:intracellular_atp:negat.mechanism: Allosteric negative feedback: excess ATP binds to an allosteric site on PFK (outside the fructose-6-phosphate active site), conformationally inhibiting the enzyme and blocking glycolysis

causal:influence:isovaleryl_coa_dehydrog.evidence: Isovaleric acidemia (IVD, OMIM 243500); Tanaka & Rosenberg, Eur. J. Pediatr. 1983 (PMID 6452974): 4-hydroxyisovaleric acid identified as new metabolite in isovaleric acidemia; Leoncini et al., Clin. causal:influence:isovaleryl_coa_dehydrog.mechanism: Isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase (IVD) dehydrogenates isovaleryl-CoA in leucine catabolism; IVD deficiency accumulates isovaleryl-CoA and free isovaleric acid, which undergoes omega-oxidation to 4-hydroxyisovaleric acid — reduced IVD activity raises urinary 4-hydroxyisovaleric acid

causal:influence:lchad_mtp_activity:nega.evidence: LCHAD/MTP deficiency (OMIM 609016): Frontiers Pediatrics 2021 PMC8017228 ('eight analytes including C16:1-OH used in screening'); Orphanet ORPHA:5; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine | intervention: loss-of-function of HADHA gene (LCHAD/MTP deficiency, OMIM 609016)
causal:influence:lchad_mtp_activity:nega.mechanism: LCHAD (HADHA subunit of MTP) oxidizes long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA substrates including 3-hydroxypalmitoleoyl-CoA (C16:1-OH-CoA); reduced activity causes 3-hydroxypalmitoleoylcarnitine (C16:1-OH) to accumulate in plasma; C16:1-OH is one of the eight diagnostic analytes used in newborn screening for LCHAD/MTP deficiency

causal:influence:lean_body_mass:positive.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-139 (24.3: Carbohydrate Metabolism): 'Changes in body composition, including reduced lean muscle mass, are mostly responsible for this decrease [in metabolic rate]'
causal:influence:lean_body_mass:positive.mechanism: skeletal muscle (lean mass) is the dominant site of resting energy expenditure; loss of muscle mass directly reduces whole-body basal metabolic rate

causal:influence:lsec_ha_clearance_rate:.evidence: Burtis & Ashwood Tietz Textbook (serum HA as a marker of liver fibrosis; LSECs as the principal site of HA clearance); Harris & Weigel 2008 (stabilin-2/HARE is the major HA receptor responsible for systemic HA clearance in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells); Grigorescu et al. 2006 (hyaluronic acid concentration in liver diseases, PMC5063891); Shen et al. 2023 (hyaluronin in liver fibrosis: LSEC capillarisation and stabilin-2 downregulation reduce HA uptake, PMC10027054). | intervention: do(LSEC dysfunction/loss) in CCl4 liver injury model — LSEC capillarisation and stabilin-2 downregulation reduces HA endocytosis, raising plasma HA.
causal:influence:lsec_ha_clearance_rate:.mechanism: Liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) express stabilin-2 (STAB2/FEEL-2/HARE) that mediates high-affinity receptor-mediated endocytosis and catabolism of circulating hyaluronic acid; LSEC-mediated clearance is the principal systemic HA disposal mechanism. When LSEC function decreases (liver fibrosis, cirrhosis — capillarisation and stabilin-2 downregulation), HA clearance falls and plasma HA rises proportionally to fibrotic burden.

causal:influence:lysyl_hydroxylase_1_act.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, collagen biosynthesis (lysyl hydroxylase, pyridinoline crosslinks). causal:influence:lysyl_hydroxylase_1_act.mechanism: PLOD1 hydroxylation of collagen lysines is required for pyridinoline crosslink formation; released crosslinks are excreted in urine as bone/connective-tissue resorption markers. PLOD1 deficiency reduces urinary pyridinoline.

causal:influence:macrophage_activation:p.evidence: PMID 23525479; “Chitotriosidase (ChT) is secreted by chronically activated macrophages in Gaucher's disease.” | do(increase macrophage activation) -> increased chitotriosidase secretion (+) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:macrophage_activation:p.mechanism: chronically/lipid-overloaded activated macrophages secrete chitotriosidase (CHIT1); the more activated the macrophage population, the higher the CSF/plasma chitotriosidase

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: PMC6091831 (MCAD deficiency, ACADM LoF, OMIM 201450; C10 decanoylcarnitine significantly elevated); GeneReviews NBK1424 (C8/C10 the primary biomarkers for MCAD deficiency in newborn screening) | intervention: ACADM LoF (MCAD deficiency, OMIM 201450)

causal:influence:mitochondrial_complex_i.evidence: BCS1L deficiency / GRACILE syndrome (OMIM 614297): BCS1L mutations abolish Complex III assembly and reduce overall respiratory chain activity in muscle/liver; respiratory chain complex III deficiency due to BCS1L mutations (PMID 28427446; PMID 19162478). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry ch. 19 (oxidative phosphorylation: complexes I-IV function in series). | intervention: do(BCS1L LoF) -> reduced Complex III activity -> reduced overall respiratory chain electron-transport flux [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:mitochondrial_complex_i.mechanism: Complex III (ubiquinol:cytochrome c oxidoreductase) transfers electrons from ubiquinol to cytochrome c; its activity is a rate-limiting step in overall mitochondrial electron transport chain flux. Loss-of-function of Complex III assembly factor BCS1L reduces Complex III activity and consequently the overall respiratory chain activity.

causal:influence:mmp2_fibroblast_activit.evidence: Multicentric osteolysis nodulosis and arthropathy (MONA, OMIM 605156): all patients lacked MMP-2 gelatinolytic activity from inactivating MMP2 mutations (Nat Genet 2001; Eur J Hum Genet 2009 PMC2721823); The Complex Role of MMP-2 in Health and Disease (PMC11728377, 2025); Plasma Levels of MMP-2 and MMP-9 in Patients with Chronic Chagas Heart Disease correlated with TGF-β (PMC10132902); Regulation of MT1-MMP/MMP-2 in cardiac fibroblasts by TGF-β1 (Cardiovasc Res 2003) | intervention: do(MMP2 LoF) — inactivating mutations → absent plasma MMP-2 gelatinolytic activity (MONA disease); do(MMP2 +) → elevated plasma MMP-2 in heart failure and hypertensive heart disease (clinical observation)

causal:influence:molecular_chaperone_act.evidence: Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-4.10.5 (Misfolding and Aggregation Summary): 'this process is usually prevented in the cell by the interaction of nascent protein forms with chaperones, which sequester exposed hydrophobic patches and prevent aggregation'

NADSYN1 deficiency depletes cellular NAD+ — impairing the NADH/NAD+ redox balance and the availability of NAD+ for Complex I-dependent NADH oxidation, thus reducing Complex I flux and oxidative phosphorylation. NADSYN1 LoF → intracellular NAD+ ↓ → mitochondrial Complex I activity ↓.

causal:influence:slc39a14_activity:negat.evidence: OMIM 617013 (hypermanganesemia with dystonia 2, HMNDYT2; SLC39A14 LoF); GeneReviews NBK431123 (SLC39A14 deficiency impairs hepatic Mn uptake and biliary excretion, resulting in Mn accumulation in circulation and brain; whole-blood Mn markedly elevated >1000 nmol/L); Rojas et al. 2018 PMC5791243 (SLC39A14 mutations cause hypermanganesemia); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (hepatic manganese clearance). | intervention: SLC39A14 loss-of-function (autosomal-recessive, OMIM 617013)
causal:influence:slc39a14_activity:negat.mechanism: ZIP14 (SLC39A14) is a Mn uptake transporter expressed on hepatocytes that imports Mn from portal blood into liver cells, enabling hepatic Mn clearance via biliary excretion (through SLC30A10). When ZIP14 activity is lost, hepatocytes cannot take up plasma Mn for biliary excretion; Mn accumulates in the circulation and brain (hypermanganesemia). Intervention: do(SLC39A14 LoF) -> blood Mn rises.

causal:influence:slc6a6_activity:negativ.evidence: SLC6A6 OMIM 186854; Spandidos MMR 2020 (TauT/SLC6A6 homeostasis review); SLC6A6 G399V mutation associated with reduced taurine transport capacity (hypertaurinuria); Boron & Boulpaep (renal taurine handling). | intervention: do(SLC6A6 loss-of-function) — SLC6A6 mutation-associated hypertaurinuria [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:slc6a6_activity:negativ.mechanism: SLC6A6 (TauT) is the sodium- and chloride-dependent taurine transporter responsible for renal tubular reabsorption of taurine. Reduced SLC6A6 activity decreases taurine reabsorption, causing urinary taurine excretion to rise (hypertaurinuria). do(SLC6A6 LoF) -> urinary taurine rises.

causal:influence:sterol_27_hydroxylase_a.evidence: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / Lehninger, bile-acid synthesis; OMIM 213700 (CTX, CYP27A1)
causal:influence:sterol_27_hydroxylase_a.mechanism: CYP27A1 27-hydroxylates cholesterol/sterol intermediates (acidic bile-acid synthesis pathway); its product is 27-hydroxycholesterol.

causal:influence:succinate_dehydrogenase.evidence: Mitochondrial complex II deficiency (OMIM 252011): MRS detects high succinate peak; urine organic acids show significantly elevated succinic acid (PMC7660022); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 16 | intervention: do(SDH/SDHA loss-of-function)
causal:influence:succinate_dehydrogenase.mechanism: SDH deficiency causes succinic acid accumulation and urinary succinic aciduria — same mechanism as urinary_succinate (both are CHEBI:15741 succinic acid nodes representing the same analyte in urine)

causal:influence:tert_expression:positiv.mechanism: TERT gene encodes the catalytic reverse-transcriptase subunit of the telomerase holoenzyme; more TERT expression produces more functional telomerase enzyme

causal:influence:testosterone:positive:l.mechanism: testosterone raises LDL-cholesterol, accounting for adverse LDL:HDL ratio in men

causal:influence:trpm6_activity:positive.evidence: OMIM #602014 hypomagnesemia 1, intestinal (TRPM6); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (DCT magnesium reabsorption); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
causal:influence:trpm6_activity:positive.mechanism: TRPM6 is the apical Mg2+ entry channel of the distal convoluted tubule that mediates active transcellular magnesium reabsorption; TRPM6 loss-of-function causes renal magnesium wasting (and impairs intestinal Mg2+ absorption)

causal:influence:tsh:positive:tpo_nis_or.evidence: "TSH increases NIS, Tg, and TPO synthesis and iodine organification and Tg turnover." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 11 (thyroid hormone synthesis / organification)
causal:influence:tsh:positive:tpo_nis_or.mechanism: TSH acts on follicular-cell TSHR (quality: plasma TSH → disposition: TSHR/cAMP signalling → process: increased NIS/Tg/TPO synthesis and iodide organification → quality: TPO/NIS organification capacity)

causal:influence:uroporphyrinogen_decarb.evidence: Harrison's PIM, The Porphyrias (PCT: elevated plasma uroporphyrin); ASH Education Program 2024 (PCT: plasma porphyrins elevated, predominantly uroporphyrin). OMIM 176100 (familial PCT, UROD LoF). | intervention: UROD loss-of-function (porphyria cutanea tarda, OMIM 176100)
causal:influence:uroporphyrinogen_decarb.mechanism: UROD deficiency (PCT) causes hepatic accumulation of uroporphyrin (the oxidised form of the 8-COOH uroporphyrinogen substrate), which spills into plasma. Plasma uroporphyrin is elevated in PCT and used diagnostically.

causal:influence:vlcad_activity:negative.evidence: GeneReviews NBK6816 (VLCAD deficiency, OMIM 201475; C12:1 listed among most often abnormal acylcarnitines; C14:1/C12:1 ratio is a diagnostic marker); MDPI Metabolomics 2023 PMC10301765 | intervention: ACADVL LoF (VLCAD deficiency, OMIM 201475)
causal:influence:vlcad_activity:negative.mechanism: VLCAD LoF causes C12:1 dodecenoyl-CoA accumulation (C12:1 is among the acylcarnitines most often abnormal in VLCAD deficiency, used in C14:1/C12:1 diagnostic ratio); dodecenoylcarnitine (C12:1) is elevated in plasma in VLCAD deficiency

causal:influence:vlcad_activity:negative.evidence: GeneReviews NBK6816 (VLCAD deficiency, OMIM 201475; C16 palmitoylcarnitine elevated); Springer JIMD 1996 (effect of fasting/fat load on long-chain acylcarnitines including C16 in VLCAD deficiency) | intervention: ACADVL LoF (VLCAD deficiency, OMIM 201475)
causal:influence:vlcad_activity:negative.mechanism: VLCAD oxidizes palmitoyl-CoA (C16) during long-chain mitochondrial beta-oxidation; LoF causes palmitoyl-CoA accumulation and conjugation to carnitine as palmitoylcarnitine (C16, CHEBI:17490); elevated C16 palmitoylcarnitine is part of the VLCAD deficiency acylcarnitine profile and also elevated in CPT2/CACT deficiency

causal:influence:xanthine_oxidase_activi.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (xanthine oxidase substrates); hereditary xanthinuria OMIM 278300 (XDH deficiency -> xanthine accumulation, hypouricemia); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology
causal:influence:xanthine_oxidase_activi.mechanism: xanthine and hypoxanthine are the substrates consumed by xanthine oxidoreductase; higher XO activity consumes them faster, lowering plasma xanthine/hypoxanthine (XDH deficiency reverses this -> xanthinuria)
